Question ID: GEO_U02_L05_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.RP.1

If M is the midpoint of AB, what can you conclude?

feedback.text: The whole segment is not congruent to one part.
Correct. A midpoint divides a segment into two congruent parts.

answer.text: A, M, and B form a right angle.

feedback.text: Midpoint describes segment lengths, not right angles.
A midpoint lies on the segment.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U02_L05_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.RP.1

If two angles form a linear pair, what is true?

feedback.text: Linear pair angles are not always equal.
That describes complementary angles.
Vertical angles are opposite, not adjacent.
Correct. A linear pair forms a straight angle.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U02_L05_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.RP.1

Which reason supports congruent opposite angles from intersecting lines?

feedback.text: Correct. Vertical angles are congruent.
Segment addition concerns lengths.
Midpoint concerns segments.
Reflexive means an object is congruent to itself.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U02_L05_Q04

If ray BD bisects angle ABC, what is supported?

feedback.text: Angle bisectors do not prove side congruence.
Bisecting does not make the whole angle right.
Correct. An angle bisector creates two congruent angles.

answer.text: D is the midpoint of AC

feedback.text: An angle bisector does not necessarily create a midpoint.
